subject: MSA redline: service title vs usage rights — proposed path
messages:
From: Erin Collins <erin.collins@helioworks.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@helioworks.com, legal@helioworks.com
Date: Wed, 21 Oct 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: MSA redline — Clarifying output title and training use

Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo last week — HelioWorks is excited about Redwood’s latency profile. Our legal team attached a marked MSA (HelioWorks_MSA_Redline_v2.pdf) with three clauses that need clarification before procurement signs off:

1) Section 2.4 (Output ownership): asks that any outputs generated by HelioWorks prompts be assigned to HelioWorks.
2) Section 6.1 (Training/Use of Customer Content): requests an explicit prohibition on using HelioWorks prompts or outputs to improve or train Redwood models, plus an obligation to delete any cached KV or prefixes.
3) New Exhibit E (Feedback license): proposes a perpetual license for any feedback HelioWorks gives to Redwood for product improvements.

From our side, procurement wants clear language and evidence of operational controls (KV eviction, logs). Can you confirm whether Redwood can:
- Provide a short, auditable statement of how prefix/KV caching is scoped and deleted?
- Offer a limited training carve-out (e.g., aggregated/non-identifiable telemetry only) instead of blanket prohibition?

I've cc'ed procurement and legal so we can keep everything thread-visible. If you prefer, we can do a 30-minute sync with your legal and engineering ops to walk through the operational controls.

Attachments: HelioWorks_MSA_Redline_v2.pdf (pdf)

--
Erin Collins
Head of Procurement | HelioWorks
procurement@helioworks.com

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 21 Oct 2026 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: MSA redline — Clarifying output title and training use

Laura / Ben — forwarding HelioWorks’ redlines. High level notes from my side:

- Output ownership: HelioWorks is pushing for assignment of outputs. That’s not how we normally operate for hosted APIs; we grant customers broad rights to outputs but we can’t assign title to us (Redwood needs rights to use aggregated telemetry to maintain the service).
- Training prohibition: they want a hard ban. We can offer a strict opt-out of training using customer-provided prompts/outputs (per-deal setting), plus an operational attest that we do not feed identifiable customer content into model training pipelines. We should define what "aggregate telemetry" means in the doc (tokens/latency/anon perf traces).
- Feedback license: their suggested perpetual license is too broad; propose a limited, non-exclusive license for improvements limited to non-confidential, anonymized feedback for two years.

Ask: Laura, can you draft redline language that accomplishes: 1) a carve-out for per-deal training opt-out (customer-controlled), 2) express representations about cache eviction and KV handling, and 3) a narrower feedback license limited in scope/duration?

I’d like to keep procurement in the loop — HelioWorks timeline looks like EOW decision if we can move quickly. We may also offer a securityOps call to show deletion logs / KV eviction runbook.

Thanks,
Karthik
Head of Sales, Enterprise
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: MAP-of-rights.xlsx (xlsx) — internal assessment]

From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 22 Oct 2026 10:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: MSA redline — Clarifying output title and training use

Karthik + Ben —

Thanks for the context. I’ve drafted three short redline excerpts (attached as Suggested_MSAText_komments.docx) that I think protect Redwood’s productization needs while giving HelioWorks commercial comfort. Key elements: 

1) Output clause (proposed):
- We can add an express statement: "Customer retains ownership of Customer Content and Outputs to the extent provided by applicable law; Redwood grants Customer an exclusive, perpetual, worldwide right to use Outputs for Customer’s internal business purposes."
- Add a reciprocal note that Redwood retains the right to use aggregated, de-identified Outputs for service improvement and diagnostics.

2) Training/Use carve-out:
- Offer a per-contract opt-out toggle: "Customer may elect to opt out of use of Customer Content and Outputs for model training or improvement; Redwood shall implement the opt-out within 7 business days and provide a remediation report confirming removal of any cached KV associated with Customer requests."
- Include an operational definition: "KV/prefix caches are considered ephemeral; Redwood maintains logs of eviction events for 12 months and will provide evidence under NDA."

3) Feedback license:
- Counter with: "Any Feedback provided by Customer shall be subject to a non-exclusive, royalty-free license to Redwood for internal product improvement purposes only, limited to two (2) years from the date Feedback is provided, and excluding Confidential Information."

I think the opt-out + evidence + limited feedback license will be acceptable. We should also prep a brief Ops checklist and screenshots from our cache eviction job to share in the call. Ben — can you own the securityOps demo and schedule a 30-min call with HelioWorks legal + procurement?

If they push for assignment of Outputs, we should propose the exclusive-rights compromise above (granting them broad internal rights, not assignment).

Laura Bennett
Counsel, Commercial Contracts | Redwood Inference

[Attachment: Suggested_MSAText_komments.docx (docx)]

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: Erin Collins <erin.collins@helioworks.com>, legal@helioworks.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 23 Oct 2026 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MSA redline — Clarifying output title and training use

Erin / HelioWorks team —

Thanks for the clear redline. We reviewed internally and propose the following path to close this quickly:

1) Output ownership: Redwood will not accept assignment of title. Instead, we propose an explicit clause granting HelioWorks an exclusive, perpetual, worldwide right to use Outputs for HelioWorks’ internal business purposes, with Redwood retaining the right to use aggregated and de-identified Outputs for platform improvement.

2) Training/Use: Redwood will implement a per-contract opt-out for training/use of Customer Content and Outputs. If HelioWorks elects the opt-out, Redwood will: 
- Flag the account at the routing layer to exclude the data from any model training pipelines;
- Execute a KV eviction for prefixes associated with the customer within 7 business days;
- Provide an operational remediation report under NDA showing eviction events and evidence logs.

3) Feedback: We can accept a non-exclusive, royalty-free license limited to internal product improvement for two (2) years and excluding Confidential Information.

Next steps: Laura has attached suggested wording — if that’s acceptable to HelioWorks, Ben will run a brief runbook demo (30 minutes) to show how KV eviction and logs work, and we’ll provide the remediation report template. Can we schedule the call early next week?

If HelioWorks still insists on assignment of outputs, please flag that early — we will escalate to execs but assignment will be a major commercial deviation.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Sales, Enterprise | Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com

[Attachments: Suggested_MSAText_komments.docx; MAP-of-rights.xlsx]
